cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-18
cards.text: 10-18 Fully automatic: build fixes and features without approval, then report in plain words. Decide, then tell (one line, so he can reverse it); ask only when a choice is truly his.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-18
cards.text: 10-18 Never idle: never wait on another thread, a check or a merge; start the next independent item. Threads keep working overnight; a morning summary is not a stopping point (11-11).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-18
cards.text: 10-18 Only what the task needs in context; helpers get only the files and checks they need and return short reports.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 The right model and effort per task: the strongest model at high effort or more for design, architecture, the kit, anything across apps and anything that regressed before; lighter tiers only for mechanical work; always set both; do small jobs yourself. (Fable only for the hardest work, 11-11.)

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-19
cards.text: 10-19 Concrete work only: no general polish sweeps; walk the screens you changed.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-20
cards.text: 10-20 Prune whole: what goes is deleted everywhere (code, tests, help, proxy, data); no off flags, no backward-compatibility code, nothing kept "in case". Refactor freely while the tests pass.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 No legacy forwards or back-compat: a page, route or file lives at one address; when it moves, the old address is deleted, never forwarded (no redirect, no second copy). No code for an old kit, an old API shape, an old storage key or an old host once its week is up. The only things kept: what people's saved data still needs to read (their books, accounts, timetables, sign-ins until they run out), and the installed standalone apps (Money's home-screen app keeps working with its data).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-30
cards.text: 10-30 "Faster" means a substantial, measured improvement: find where the wait really goes, cut it structurally, report before/after times.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-23
cards.text: 10-23 Secrets stay sealed in Cloudflare/GitHub; never ask Jay to dig up keys. While he's away or quota is out: don't ask, wait for the reset and resume.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 A finished round's report is a new document written from scratch, each point led by before → after numbers; never the old one with dated sections stacked on (his recap too, 11-10), never 「新」 marks.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-11
cards.text: 11-11 Threads: resolve one as soon as its work is done and checked, rename it to its current scope, reuse an existing thread for a repeat; do related work together in one thread.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-01
cards.text: 11-01 Only main exists in every repo: no branches, no PRs, never the session's claude/... branch even when a session's setup asks. Push with sh ../Orbit-Core/tools/push.sh (in Orbit-Core sh tools/push.sh) and nothing else (10-21, 10-22: never ask before pushing, kit included).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 No "run failed" emails: push.sh rebases onto origin/main (10-21: never push a tree from an old checkout; a stale push once wiped Law's 裁判), runs what the deploy runs (the repo's tests against main's kit, Class's build) and pushes only when they pass. Nothing more (11-15, Jay: "I want fast pushing that things go live as fast as it could"): every app's tests and the layout check are run by hand when wanted.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-22
cards.text: 10-22 Kit order: Orbit-Core first, wait for pages.yml, then the apps; never a cancelling concurrency: in a workflow (copy the queue job); builds check out main's tip.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-22
cards.text: 10-22 Orbit-Securities: after a push, confirm its deploy started; if not, run deploy.yml by hand. Every thread confirms its deploy went green.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-19
cards.text: 10-19 No separate test step and no Mac gate: check your own cloud screenshots (WebKit), push, Jay tests on his phone.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-01
cards.text: 11-01 Every site is on Cloudflare under Jay's domain; GitHub keeps the code only (Pages off). A job that fetches or serves data runs in a Worker (edge cache, the existing crons, a Durable Object alarm), never a workflow writing to git. Actions keep build, test, deploy and only what Cloudflare can't do, writing to Cloudflare, never the repo; all inside the free plans, anything that could pass them put to Jay first.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 Never reorder an app's tabs or change the tab it opens on without asking (Transit opens on 地圖).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Anything two apps use lives in the Orbit-Core kit, never copied; look first (node tools/kit-find.mjs <word>, --apps finds copies) and move duplicates there when you see them. 11-03 Apps stay thin: device storage, Pass sync, patching a screen in place and every shared piece are the kit's; an app keeps only what is truly its own.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-11
cards.text: 11-11 One structure, nothing twice, short enough to read before every task: the layout is in Orbit-Core's CLAUDE.md. Each fact has one home and is linked elsewhere; a doc is updated in the same push as the change that made it wrong; no plans or logs in repos (the git log is the history). 11-14 The one handoff is HANDOFF.md: how a new workspace or agent starts, what lives outside git (accounts, secrets by name, data, schedules); updated in the push that adds an account, a secret or a schedule.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 Orbit-Core's MAP.md names every part of the architecture so nothing is built twice.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-18
cards.text: 10-18 As real as Taiwan: real brokers, buses, trains, TV; remove what isn't real, add what is.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-20
cards.text: 10-20 One quality, one family: every app works and feels the same. Chinese (Traditional, Taiwan) first, in Taiwan's words; English second.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 Orbit (/app/, kit suite.mjs): every app in one home-screen app, to become the main way to use Orbit. Never called a "portal" on screen. It feels like the separate apps (no grid of tiles): tabs across apps with an animated switch, never a white flash (11-14, every case in docs/ORBIT.md), every cross-app feature opening in place. A separate app may suggest Orbit at a hop to another app, always declinable, never nagging.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-15
cards.text: 11-15 No separate apps (Jay: "the link … of individual app should still open that app in orbit, not the standalone app, make standalone app no more"): every app's address (orbit.jaypengx.com/sports/, a notice, an old home-screen icon) opens in Orbit at that app (kit suite.mjs alone); on a phone's browser that is Orbit's add page. Only our tools, another page's frame (the Showcase's demos) or ?solo see an app alone. The website, Showcase and every README point to Orbit.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Many Orbits: before Add to Home Screen, an optional setup picks which apps and which icon (many to choose from); a person may add several Orbits for different purposes, single-app ones too. Setup is never required. For new people a single-app Orbit replaces the separate apps; separate apps already on a home screen keep working. Orbit's address shows the app on screen, never the setup; how each case behaves: docs/ORBIT.md 18–23.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Every notice banner is one kind (kit noticeLife): the same 5 s on screen (a touch gives it 5 s more), swiped up to take it away (11-14: up only, never dragged about), gone on a scroll or a tap elsewhere. Jay: "unify … all can be swiped off, all stay the same amount of time".

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 Orbit keeps every app opened running: switching back never loads it again, and an app playing sound (Beats) is never closed however many apps are opened after it.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 Where Orbit opens: an app with something live (a trip, a rental, a bus alert, 專注飛行, Beats playing) on that screen; else, back to an Orbit the phone kept, the last app if left under an hour ago; else (and always after Orbit was closed) the app list, last app on top, every app at its start. Orbit Pass sign-in comes first.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-21
cards.text: 10-21 AI editors can do anything the app can do by hand. 10-21 Never blame the network for a slow AI or a failed update.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-20
cards.text: 10-20 Real logos and headshots, never letter tiles; pictures for everything that has one. 10-20 First-tap bugs are bugs: a button never needs two taps.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-21
cards.text: 10-21 Stats show the current season; last season only where this one is empty. 10-21 Past-game pages show only that game's data. 10-21 One layout per page across states (before, live, after). 10-21 Reflect results the moment they happen: never hide data because a feed is stale; compute from live results.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-21
cards.text: 10-21 No cross-app spending pop-ups; notification permission asked at most once.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-23
cards.text: 10-23 Every team name in Chinese; people in their own English names in both languages; never transliterate.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-23
cards.text: 10-23 A typhoon day off (停班停課) acts like a holiday in every app (kit dayoff.mjs).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 One app order everywhere the apps are listed: Sports, Transit, Weather, Class, Money, News, Words, Beats, Law, Securities (kit APP_ORDER, never a list of its own; Securities, the play-money game, last).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 One language at a time: every page all Chinese or all English by the Orbit language; names in English where a source has them (kit place()); only what has no English stays Chinese, marked lang="zh-Hant". tools/gate.mjs flags mixed.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 A full Chinese and a full English Orbit (Jay): everything a person reads is in the Orbit language, the world's stories in Chinese and Taiwan's in English too. What the AI writes it writes in the reader's language (never translated after); what it doesn't (an outlet's own headline or summary) goes through plain translation, Google's free month (translate.js, a hard cap under 500k characters, each text once), never the AI. A foreign person's name stays in English, never a guessed Chinese one; one Taiwan always writes one way (川普, 黃仁勳, 賴清德) is written that way.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 No guard for people outside Taiwan: no country, clock or GPS checks, nothing closed abroad. English for a phone that lists no Chinese; 'today' by the phone's clock. °C and NT$ only.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 A permission is asked when it's needed, never blocking; saying no never closes an app (it falls back). Location when an app opens on where you are (Transit's map, Weather), else on a tap; the compass only from a tap on 我的位置, once a launch, never after a no; the microphone on 錄音; notices on a switch or a tapped 允許. An answer is remembered.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 Links out: iOS's quick view stays the default; one Pass switch (連結 › Safari App, following the pass everywhere) sends every app's links to Safari itself (kit linkHref/openLink). Links into other apps (YouTube, Maps, 高鐵 T Express) are iOS's either way; 高鐵訂票 offers T Express first.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Addresses: every app at orbit.jaypengx.com/<short> (one origin, one Pass sign-in), the proxy at api.jaypengx.com, the bare jaypengx.com Jay's own homepage (handle JayPengX only: no real name or school; no betting; open to all) with the showcase at /showcase/. Clean breaks, no redirects.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-20
cards.text: 10-20 The loading screen lifts once, onto finished content, fast; nothing pops in after. 11-03 It lifts only after the opening's update check answered (at most 3 s past the app's readiness, at once offline: kit boot.js).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 An update opens on its first opening, as fast as it can, never "next time": on a link that answered quickly the service worker opens the server's page itself; on a slow one the kept page opens and the 11-03 hold stands. A page already open is never swapped in front of the person: it swaps as they come back after 5 minutes away.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-20
cards.text: 10-20 Slow internet must work: hashed files, nothing downloaded twice, no cache wipe on update.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-01
cards.text: 11-01 Smooth in everything: a tap answers in the same frame; a sheet opens at once on what's known, shimmering places the size of what comes. 11-03 Instant everywhere: a screen paints at once on what the phone or the edge has and refreshes behind (stale-while-revalidate, never for a live number shown as live); a tap shows its result at once and settles when the server answers (undone with a word if it fails); what the person opens next is read ahead while idle, from the edge's cache, never a paid call.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-01
cards.text: 11-01 A live update never moves the page; apps patch in place, never rebuild what didn't change; live beats wait while a finger is down. 11-03 Nothing jumps from the person's own taps either: a tapped control stays under the finger; a sized sheet never shrinks under the finger; a list being read is drawn as rows the size of those coming, never "none" before the day's reads are in. 11-03 A part read after the rest holds its place from the first drawing (kit waiting(shape); Sports' later()), never a card popping in above what's read.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-05
cards.text: 11-05 A live page holds still in Safari too: only a scroll the code asks for may move a held place; a scroll nobody made is put back. 11-05 Dragging iOS's scroll bar moves the page smoothly. Check with node tools/live-scroll.mjs <app> --webkit. 10-21 Test UI in WebKit, not only Chromium.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-05
cards.text: 11-05 A tab you come back to is as you left it (place and drawing); a detail tapped in one tab opens over that tab, the same way for every kind.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-21
cards.text: 10-21 The keyboard never pushes content off screen; the iPhone's own keyboard, never an in-app keypad (kit watchKeyboard). Input bars sit above the keyboard. 11-11 A field takes the keys right the first time (Jay: "I often need to click on a typing field then close it then opens again to have a perfect focus … in the kit so every typing field gets it"): a field about to be typed in first ends any movement carrying it (a sheet's slide: iOS placed the caret mid-slide, under the screen), the keys are read again once they settle (kit landField, watchKeyboard); a sheet opened to be typed in focuses its field in the tap that opened it, never a frame or a timer later.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 One tab bar in every app: the kit's floating capsule; an in-progress bar is a .q-accessory pill above it. 10-30 It stays whole while scrolling; the round action beside it is smaller than the bar, on its middle.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-05
cards.text: 11-05 A swipe up to leave the app never picks a tab: a touch in the strip along the screen's foot picks only when the finger lifts; the bar stays as low as iOS's own.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-22
cards.text: 10-22 One date selector in every app (kit dayBar/dayStrip). 11-06 At most a week on a wide page; 11-10 the week spans the page's width with 📅 at its end.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-31
cards.text: 10-31 A sheet never scrolls sideways (.q-sheet overflow-x: hidden; date fields appearance: none, min-width: 0). 10-21 No wraps, orphan pills, cut numbers, sideways tables or scrolling sheets. 10-20 Balanced cards at any count, long names never wrap badly.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-31
cards.text: 10-31 Never the browser's own popups: the kit's ask()/tell()/confirm(); a one-tap delete gets a 復原 toast (the admin page is the one exception left).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-31
cards.text: 10-31 Every screen, either way up: a phone upright (320–440) or on its side, a tablet, a computer, each laid out for its own space (DESIGN §10). 11-01 Wide screens show more at a glance, not a phone's view made bigger. 11-06 A computer (mouse or trackpad, 1000 px+) gets a side bar; an iPad keeps its rail. Details and the 11-06/11-11 layout rules: DESIGN §10.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-19
cards.text: 10-19 Paid AI runs only behind a person's tap, never automatically. 11-14 (Jay: "make AI feature like this a button to click like we do in orbit law, never spend a penny on AI on things user didn't interact with across app"): every AI part is the kit's quiet AI button, as Orbit Law's; opening a story, a game or a page never starts one, nor does a finger touching it, and nothing is made ahead, not even 頭條's lead stories. A tap that only shows an answer already kept for everyone costs nothing and is open to every pass.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 No AI means no trace of it (Jay: a no-AI pass "should not even feel AI features existed"): every AI button, row, card, box and section carries data-ai-tap (or .q-ai-tap), a box holding nothing else data-ai-only, its words for that person .q-no-ai; a row of buttons left with one fills the width, a tab bar with an AI action stretches over the room it leaves. Never an empty gap.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-11
cards.text: 11-11 Code first: no AI where code reads or formats reliably; numbers come from code and AI only words them.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 The server's helper (the Runner) is billed while awake: each request or alarm, then about ten seconds more. So a live beat asks no faster than its data changes (bus boards 30 s → cards 20 s; YouBike 60 s), light background work shares the routes' already-awake object, and nothing wakes it to find nothing (F1's odd minutes only while a session runs).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Nothing runs for nobody (Jay: "make sure Orbit's background tasks aren't burning our quota"): a hidden page, the phone's other app or Orbit's other tab, asks nothing (a live beat checks document.visibilityState; kit suite.mjs reports a hidden frame as hidden); a background job does only what's left (what's done is listed, not looked for again), stops at once when a source turns it away (never a wait in the Worker: its time is billed while it waits), and a paused job isn't started at all.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 AI spends only on what someone opens (Jay: "only spend it as I use it but kept fast enough"): made when a person asks for it, on the smallest model that does it well, its shape shown while it's made; never made ahead for every story, game, word or paper (11-17: what was made ahead is gone, not paused). Made on a tap is fast: no thinking for a short answer someone waits for (11-14: Haiku thought 13 s before a 3-point brief). Where code can do the work (reading a scan, a title, a tag), code does it. Why it burned is fixed first; each maker's day cap is only the safety net, and the 3-hourly watch warns before a balance runs low.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 AI gets a small code-picked digest of what the page doesn't already show (insight, never a repeat of the card); prompts are crafted and tested; it asks back with tap pickers from the person's own lists where that helps; each call's cost shows in admin.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-11
cards.text: 11-11 An AI answer is never plain text: it is drawn (kit aiAnswer: rows with icons, logos, faces, bars), with a skeleton of its shape while it's made. Names in its words are chips: a player with their face, a team with its logo.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-11
cards.text: 11-11 Every smart feature, code-only ones too, carries the Orbit AI mark (kit icons.ai, --q-ai), never a sparkle.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-11
cards.text: 11-11 A fallback is the same class from another maker (Sonnet ↔ GPT Sol for judgement, Haiku ↔ Luna for writing, Flash only for pictures and the cheapest), each answer naming its model in admin. AI makers are Anthropic, OpenAI and Google only (never DeepSeek or Qwen).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 Orbit's own look (原生 Native) in all nine apps, every page: <html data-look="native">, graphite cards, colour only on what it names, the app's colour for now and the main action (DESIGN §11). It is a UX redesign: layouts, navigation and flows may change, every feature kept.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 Orbit's own design, never another app's (Apple's Weather, Sports, Stocks or anyone's: no layout, signature piece or look). Today's dark page is the base, never a sky, photo or colour filling the screen; one colour to a surface, never two clubs' colours blended. Each home is built around the person's day and the app's content, not one template. A new look change is shown to Jay before it ships.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 One focal point a screen; weight 700 only for the focal number and large titles; the accent as a pointer (about 4 uses); chips only for taps or exceptions; one radius; 4-point spacing. Fix with design principles, change the kit, not every screen. 11-03 The accent is for meaning only (the tab you're on, live, a chart's line); buttons, numbers and strips are graphite; a home club is a small house after its name; in a game list a soft grey ★ 推薦 row marks the day's picks.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Tight spacing: 24 between sections, 16 between groups and after the focus, 8 under a line naming what follows; no gap bigger than what it separates.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-19
cards.text: 10-19 No app-name title, no intro or status lines over content: open straight onto content. Top bar: the account pill and at most one tab action; help in the Pass sheet; refresh by pull. One sheet, one empty state, one segmented control (a whole view, at most 4), chips for filters, all from the kit.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 One "more": the kit's quiet bar, never accent text. 11-03 Never an accent-coloured text link.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 No uneven grid anywhere: like tiles fill every row (fullRows, .q-rows-full; a grid to pick from keeps every item, .q-rows-keep).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 A long name stays on one line at its row's size: the short form where it fits, the room made for it, the last name alone only where nothing else fits; never smaller, never an ellipsis.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 One way to put a list in order: a grip (three lines) at the row's end, held and dragged (kit reorder + grip); never arrows or 往前/往後.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-22
cards.text: 10-22 Colour only where it means something (win or loss, a live state). 10-21 No bright white surfaces in dark mode; logos on their tile, never white plates or see-through.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-19
cards.text: 10-19 Nothing cut, no duplicates, no emoji icons, real logos, every sheet in the kit's style; check 320 and 390, light and dark, in WebKit.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-23
cards.text: 10-23 App icons: each app its own bright hue, a big white symbol over the family ring; share cards are icon, name and one line. 10-23 Avatars: 96 drawn looks, never emoji; the signed-in dot small on the rim; picking a look shows no pop-up.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Maps weighted by relevance: markers get quieter, never hidden (DESIGN §7).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-30
cards.text: 10-30 / 11-01 The tab rail is slim (60 wide), the pick a capsule hugging its tab. 11-06 It is the same in all apps and one column (tabs, round action and account one width), shaped by the kit alone.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 One layout for every screen: wide pages and sheets are built from kit pieces that read their own box, and every push runs tools/layout-check.mjs (320, iPad, laptop: no narrow band, empty half, lone shrunk card or overflow). 11-11 A wide page balances by what's in it, a heading search or total runs across the top, a grid fills rows evenly, a day strip stays one scrolling row, a picture tile at most twice its size.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 No wasted space (Jay: "empty space and disproportion"): a card is as tall as what it holds; no empty band above, below or beside content; no blank half of a row, card or screen; a quiet screen is short, never padded out. The only gaps are the spacing rule's (24/16/8); anything emptier is a bug.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 In proportion: every piece is sized for what it carries, at the kit's sizes: no bar, button or card bigger than its content needs, no icon or logo small next to the text it sits with, like pieces in a row the same size, a hero never taller than its facts need (half the screen at most on a phone on its side).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Grids of tiles keep even rows (Jay: "don't like the unbalance", 9 apps then 1 alone): the ten apps are five by two at every width (two by five only if five can't fit), never a lonely last row; any grid of apps or icons goes through kit evenGrid, which picks columns that split the tiles evenly as the width changes.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 No text wraps where it shouldn't: titles, names, numbers, buttons, chips, tags and tab labels stay on one line at 320 (the short form, or room made: the long-name rule above); running text breaks only between words or phrases, never one character or one word alone on a line.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 No old look left: anything a newer design replaced (§6 and DESIGN §11) is a bug wherever it remains: gradient or app-colour-filled cards, colour tiles, a sky or photo behind the page, two clubs' colours on one card, old sweeps and animations, a docked bar, a help pill, accent text links, sparkle AI icons, letter tiles, white logo plates, ↑↓ reorder arrows, 32 gaps, an app's own dialogs or sheets.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 Features don't explain themselves (Jay: "it explains it too much, when all it needs is one sentence or none"): a screen, card or sheet carries at most one short line of explanation, and none where the controls already say it; no paragraphs, how-it-works notes, feature tours in the page, or lines repeating what a label or picture shows. Help belongs in the Pass sheet's 說明. When adding a feature, write its words last and cut them to the fewest.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 Wording, both languages: Chinese is natural Traditional Chinese in Taiwan's words (not translated from English, no mainland terms); English is natural, plain and short (not translated from Chinese); the same thing has the same name everywhere in an app and across the family, in both; every string exists in both, means the same in both, and fits the same space; no typos, wrong measure words or mixed punctuation (full-width in Chinese, half-width in English).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 Nothing out of place: a piece that looks different from what's around it (its own font size, colour, corner, shadow, spacing, button or control shape; not built from the kit) is rebuilt from the kit's components in the family's style. If the kit lacks it, it goes into the kit, never a one-off.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-30
cards.text: 10-30 Screenshots are authentic: the world's data always live; only what a person keeps in their account comes from a demo account built by using the app. 10-27 Framing edits are fine (crop, a zoomed callout, a headline, a background), content edits never. 11-01 One set for the READMEs and the showcase, both languages, nothing used twice in a set. 10-28 Shot 1 is the app's strongest hero screen; niche or just-asked features later.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 A screenshot set sells the app (Jay: "think like a marketer"): shot 1 makes plain what the app is for; each shot after it is one main feature that makes the app special, in proportion to how central it is, never chosen for being new (the 11-11 set gave Law four 代表會 shots and Sports mostly AI). Each headline is confident and carries a real number where one sells (counted from the data, rounded so it stays true: 「5.4 萬部法規」). Every shot shows different content (another story, game, stock, word); one shot per feature; Orbit AI one shot at most, only where it is central; never a competitor's name or a comparison. The plan with each set's one-line reason: tools/shots/store.mjs.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Dark and light mixed in every set (Jay: "why is there not a mix of light and dark"; shots 1, 3, 5 dark, 2, 4, 6 light), and a shot's Chinese and English are the same screen in the same state, only the language differs (one clock, one seeded Math.random per run). Six shots so the README's rows of three come out whole: four on a phone, one on an iPad and one on a computer, so it's plain every device is supported (Jay: "mix a few computer and iPad shots").

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 Only the domain is paid: Workers Free (heavy routes and crons' work in the Runner DO), TDX free tier, Google free tiers; everything runs by itself. 11-10 AI is the one exception: billing on for Anthropic, OpenAI and Gemini, prepaid as a hard stop where offered; a blind side-by-side test picks the model. Tests and our tools count against the same free amounts.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-05
cards.text: 11-05 Never billed past what's included, and slowed only for real: the guard paces only once a count's real share passes 60/75/85% and the rate would reach the stop; a forecast is a warning in admin, never a slow-down; at 85% the basics first (sign-in, sync, notices) and nobody new let in. Paid outside APIs stop inside their free amounts (Maps at 90% of each SKU, Google Weather under its month).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 Save quota hard, never at the person's cost: every request, CPU ms, KV/R2/D1 op and outside call cut wherever the person sees the same thing as fast; measured; phone data counts too. 11-10 Phone first: whatever a phone can read itself (open to browsers, no key, no form session) the phone reads, the Worker only its fallback; the Worker keeps keyed sources, sites closed to browsers or abroad, form sessions, and pages one Worker read serves to everyone.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 Scraping is allowed: an operator's own site or app is a source like any API; dig for one before saying there's none.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Gemini is reliable, only costly: replace it only where a free path is as reliable; otherwise make calls cheaper. Every AI route has a global daily cap (D1); Google Weather is shared per 0.05° square.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 One live copy of an app: the same app open twice keeps one copy reading; the others go quiet (已在別處開啟, 在這裡繼續); nothing is lost. 10-23 All apps can run at once.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 One account, many places (Jay: "when I have a trip in orbit it won't have a trip in a standalone app"; Orbit, each separate home-screen app and each device keep their own storage). What you keep (settings, follows, saved things, progress, books) is the account's: on the Pass, and a place taken back reads the Pass's copy before it writes, never its older one over a newer. What you're in the middle of is the account's too (a trip being navigated, a YouBike rental, a bus alert, a 專注飛行): it goes to the Pass as it changes and the place that takes the app over (opening it, 在這裡繼續) goes on from where it was; ended anywhere, ended everywhere. One place runs it at a time (the 11-06 rule: the las

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Data must never be lost or corrupted; saves stay lean; kept collections get version history and nightly backups. 10-22 Removed items drop out of every total (an old device copy can't bring one back).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-18
cards.text: 10-18 No paid TheSportsDB key. 10-19 No paid membership ever.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-19
cards.text: 10-19 Orbit's economy: NT$200,000 to start, NT$10,000 every Monday, 急難紓困 NT$5,000 when worth is under 2,000, 財富等級 rewards (10× since 10-23: 300K/30K … 100M/3M). 10-22 Money lives in Securities: the Pass shows no balance; only the proxy adds money; a price or payout change is modelled in a test first and an exploit closed with a test that tries it. 11-06 Securities guards only so bad local data can't corrupt real data, not heavy fraud-proofing.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-05
cards.text: 11-05 Priority passes and a fair door: a priority pass is never held to a per-session limit and always let in (global AI caps and the guard's stop still hold); when too many are in, those in keep their place at slower refreshes and newcomers wait in line.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Usage is counted to improve Orbit, never to know who (Jay: "collect data … have users sign a policy … so we don't break laws anywhere"): counts only (kit usage.mjs), no account, device id, address, location or anything a person typed or keeps; on unless turned off (Pass › 隱私 › 使用統計, following the account; a browser's Global Privacy Control is off), a one-time quiet note on the first open (the policy only: off is in Pass › 隱私 and by mail, never a button on the note, Jay 11-14). No third-party trackers or ads, ever. What's collected, why and how long is the privacy policy (site/privacy/, with the terms site/terms/): a new kind of data, a new outside processor or a longer keep updates it

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Pass card: avatar, 里程碑 n/30, the account number's first 6 without prefix, the medal strip on one row; no money on the Pass.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Milestones: one per app, bronze, silver and gold, kept for good; 外觀 leads with what's worn, then the nearest next medal (a faint progress ring), then one row each; no locks, greyed grid or glows.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Passkeys: any number per Pass, named and removable, one for every app and the admin page (RP ID the domain); the pass and passkeys both sign in, no passkey-only mode. Every sign-in is a form password managers fill. 11-14 An account with no passkey is nudged by a brief quiet banner (加入 / 不再顯示, at most every 3 days on a device, gone in seconds; 不再顯示 kept for the account), never a dialog.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 The pass is stored hashed slow and peppered; no lockouts. 11-03 A pass the owner issued is replaced at its first sign-in (required, enforced by the Worker), then a passkey is offered (以後再說 skips it); passes in use are never asked.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 One account a person (Jay: "make sure in all our ways we don't accident encourage duplicating account"): nothing nudges toward a second account. 建立 shows only on the sign-in screen (never to a device signed in, never as a way around a limit); a device that was signed in before points to finding that pass first; another Orbit or app on the device reuses the sign-in already there; anything given per account (an AI allowance) needs a proved email, so a new account never gets it twice.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Recovery email: a Pass may link one email, proved by a code mailed to it; a lost pass is recovered by a code to it, then replaced at once. Never tells whether an address is on a Pass. A quiet tip suggests adding one (every 3 days at most, 不再顯示 for good), never on the open the passkey tip showed.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Invites (Jay: "Retire it but design a way for QR code to easily go to a place where people can create pass and start using"): admin 工具 › 邀請 QR code, a link and a printable QR to Orbit's sign-up (/app/?join opens 建立 at once, on a device not signed in). The giveaway (/key/, 11-05) is gone, page and all (no forward: Jay 11-14, no legacy forwarding).

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Anyone makes an Orbit Pass on any sign-in screen (建立新的 Orbit Pass) with an email proved by a code mailed to it (Jay: "Make email link mandatory for free account"), which is the pass's recovery email from the start; one account an address (an address already on a Pass is offered 用救援信箱找回, never a second account); open only once mail reaches anyone, as many a day as 設定 › Orbit Pass allows (0 closes it). Accounts without an email are asked to add one (the quiet tip), never made to. Two levels (Jay: "created pass have no AI feature or anything that eat up billing"): 基本, a pass made in an app, every app but nothing that costs money (no AI call is ever started for it; an AI answer already kep

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Orbit AI allowances (Jay: "AI allowance should be able to be set for all account, existing account and limit or duration, just give me options"; "free account still have 0 as default"): how many AI answers an account may have made a day, a month or in all, until a date or with no end, set in admin for a level (完整 50 a day, 基本 0 by default), for one account, or for every account there is now. Counted only when a model is asked for that person (an answer kept for everyone is free); 基本 gets any only with a verified email. The phone shows what's left in one quiet line on the Orbit Pass sheet; used up, the tap says so calmly.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 One sign-in: every app and Orbit show the same screen (Orbit's mark with the apps circling it, "Orbit", Orbit's colour); no app has a sign-in look of its own. A signed-out standalone app shows it and goes on in the app.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-15
cards.text: 11-15 Each app's data is locked on the phone before it syncs (end to end; Jay: "prevent from our cloud be able to read the detail"; "no way to lose data unless the pass is actually lost"): one data key an account, kept on the Pass only locked by a key made from the Orbit Pass (PBKDF2, 600,000 rounds), held by each signed-in device; the Pass typed once opens it on a new device; a new pass locks it again; the recovery email brings everything back, nothing locked or missing (Jay: "seamless"): a recovery copy of the key sealed by a Worker secret, never in the database, opened only for a recovery email's session (docs/PRIVACY.md); the database, its backups and the admin page never read anyone's d

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-15
cards.text: 11-15 Scrolling is the phone's own: every page and sheet bounces natively at both ends, never a bounce or give made by hand (Jay: "do not ever try to fake a bounce cause it never work, give back to native one"). The pull to refresh only reads the native pull. A scroll bar's handle dragged past the top is left as iOS does it.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 The admin panel is laid out around what Jay checks: 總覽, 帳戶, 使用 (11-14), 健康, 額度, 設定, 工具; plain words, no legacy jargon, money in NT$ (US$ only typing a provider's balance). The money is a sheet (證券的錢) from 總覽, not a tab; a gone app is never shown or counted.

cards.title: Orbit (shared) rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 健康 › 外部來源 shows every outside source's health (a row each: state, last success, 24 h calls and failures, where it's read, data age, quota), counted from calls the apps make anyway; a new source gets its row in kit/sources.mjs in the same push.

cards.title: Transit rule, 2026-10-22
cards.text: 10-22 YouBike is crucial: never plan a trip without bikes as a fallback; make it load reliably instead. 10-30 YouBike shows its own logo everywhere but the map (whose pins keep the bike glyph); 一般, 電輔車 and 空位 are counted apart.

cards.title: Transit rule, 2026-10-23
cards.text: 10-23 Operators' 停駛 notices are rules: what isn't running comes from their notices, never guessed; stopped services are never planned; a notice saying 部分, 減班 or a time of day is shown, never a stop; likely-off is 可能停駛, never 停駛. On a nothing-running day the app still works and says what's stopped.

cards.title: Transit rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 A trip's legs fit one line (tighten, never wrap); 查時刻 is visual (a journey bar, live 準點/晚, the next train lit), not text.

cards.title: Transit rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 Google's places on the map keep Google's own colours; a tap on one opens it at once. Google's own bus stops stay off (ours have live times). A place's or spot's card shows the YouBike near it, never its bus stops.

cards.title: Transit rule, 2026-10-29
cards.text: 10-29 偏好電輔車 is a per-trip choice on the plans card (of stations about as near, the one with 電輔車, ridden at their pace); 11-04 also a setting in 我的 › 規劃, off by default (on, every trip starts with it and station cards count 電輔車 first).

cards.title: Transit rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 Buses run early or late, trains on time: at a bus stop 5 minutes before its timetable time, 2 before a bus seen live; trains as timed; ranking unchanged, only the leave time. A bus TDX sees arriving is that timetable run: once it's gone before you can be there, the next run you can make; never 快一點 when hurrying can't make it (趕不上了).

cards.title: Transit rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 Trains go beyond TPASS: inside a TPASS area the list and planner keep to the pass's trains, but any 台鐵 or 高鐵 train can be the one you hold a ticket for (指定車次, or 用這班規劃路線 from 查時刻); 查時刻 has 全部班次.

cards.title: Transit rule, 2026-11-04
cards.text: 11-04 A train you pick is the train you take: a later departure chosen is never switched to a sooner one by itself; a plan you didn't pick still moves to a sooner train still to come (10-28). 11-13: found on another train than planned, the picks after it no longer hold (a ticket's train does): the changes after it move to the ones that train makes.

cards.title: Transit rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 追公車 (a YouBike to a stop further along a bus's way) is offered only when clearly sooner (8+ minutes, more for a long ride), with real room at the stop (4+ minutes), never on a stopped feed; once shown, the near or further stop keeps showing until the other is 10 minutes sooner. Planning only: never while navigating or replanning under way. (Replaced 11-03's 3 minutes.)

cards.title: Transit rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 Trip results never change under the person: the plans card and 交通's trips show the whole plan once (the skeleton or a trip's last ways until then); after that a way keeps its place and labels and only its times update; a way found later joins quietly at the end.

cards.title: Beats rule, 2026-10-21
cards.text: 10-21 Songs must sound clearly different. 11-10 (V21) Each song grows its own chord loops, bar rhythms and hook harmony; a song's last ring stays with its song.

cards.title: Beats rule, 2026-10-23
cards.text: 10-23 Easy listening: keep eased() (a shelf over 7 kHz, a dip at 3.2 kHz as deep as the song is sharp) and the quieter master (-15 dBFS RMS); no choir beds or glassy doublings.

cards.title: Beats rule, 2026-10-30
cards.text: 10-30 (V19) Each kind of music its own: a song opens its groove's way; nothing over C6; real instruments first (a groove's first-listed three times as often, chimes and synths a quarter); each genre its own grammar.

cards.title: Beats rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 (V20) Musical, not just in key: no held or on-beat note grinds a half step against its chord; the tune over its chords; a tune has a form (a motif, its sequence, a high point late, question and answer: tune(), FORMS).

cards.title: Beats rule, 2026-11-10

cards.title: Beats rule, 2026-11-11

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Never invent entries, balances or categories the person didn't give. Jay started fresh 2026-11-01; never re-add the 天天記帳 import or commit his CSV.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Every change to what entries mean works on what's already logged (old books upgraded on open, upgradeBooks). Removing an account never loses history.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 退款 is never income: it comes off its spend, all or part; a friend's share of what you paid comes off too, their cash counted once handed over. A 自動加值 nobody in the books paid for (a parent's card) is 收入.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Fees (ATM, 境外交易手續費) are typed from the bill, with a 1.5% tap for a credit card; never calculated on their own.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 LINE Points (any points or gift card) can pay part of a spend. 悠遊卡/一卡通 are 儲值卡, never 電子錢包.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 A card that reloads itself (自動加值): when an earlier spend on it is added, changed or deleted, every later spend is run again in date order and each reload worked out afresh, so the balance is always right and never below zero because of the order the edits came in.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-30
cards.text: 10-30 Cards carry their network (卡別: Visa, Mastercard, JCB, American Express, UnionPay…), picked when adding or editing and shown wherever the card is (its real mark).

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Ways to pay show their own logos; 手機條碼 stays black on white in dark mode.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Categories have subs and are the person's to edit (add, rename, hide, merge); 自動帶入 is set per person, never hardcoded.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-11-01
cards.text: 11-01 One set for everyone: twelve broad spending categories, two to four broad subs each (餐飲 早餐/午餐/晚餐/飲料點心; 交通 TPASS/搭車/長途/汽機車, YouBike, 捷運, 公車 and 計程車 all under 搭車; 購物 服飾美妝/3C 家電/日用品; 居住 房租房貸/水電瓦斯/電信網路/管理修繕; 娛樂 休閒/旅遊/運動; 數位; 醫療 看診/藥品/保險; 學習; 人情; 家人 孝親/育兒/寵物; 稅費; 其他). What was logged under an old set moves once, amounts untouched.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-11-01
cards.text: 11-01 Meals stay three: 早餐/午餐/晚餐 apart; 宵夜 counts as 晚餐; no 三餐 sub. 11-03 No 聚餐 sub: a meal out counts as its meal.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-31
cards.text: 10-31 Subs stay broad, because 統計 is built on them. 數位 (digital things: domains, AI plans, cloud, games) has four: 專案維運 (a project's running costs: TDX, domains, hosting), 工具訂閱, 影音串流, 遊戲. Upkeep and fun stay apart.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 記一筆: the amount is a field (the iPhone's keys, no keypad of our own); every category in view, no pages to swipe; something not set shows nothing (no example values). 預算 sits in 更多 until one is set, then in 統計.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-30
cards.text: 10-30 記一筆 guesses kind, category, sub and way to pay from the person's own entries (time of day, weekday/weekend, place when allowed, past picks); the amount is only offered and fills on a tap. Location is opt-in (更多 › 智慧帶入), kept to about 100 m.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 The guesses must be right far more often: a first week guesses from the hour as most people live it until their own entries outweigh it; a catch-up goes through the day in order; pay and bills on their day of the month; 智慧帶入's 猜中 counts only guesses made the current way. Any change is measured first: TZ=Asia/Taipei node scripts/backtest-guess.mjs --against <ref>.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 轉帳 shows only what a transfer has: the amount, 從 and 到 (logo and balance, a swap), the day, 手續費, a note; it opens on the accounts usually moved between.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-31
cards.text: 10-31 No 發票 features (no 對獎, 手機條碼, scanner or 載具 file): one 拍照記帳 for any picture (receipt, invoice, bill, app screenshot, transfer notice, price tag); the AI reads amount, day, store, items, category and way to pay; it opens as a filled entry to check, and a matching entry already logged (same amount, within a day) is offered to merge, never added twice.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 拍照記帳 reads a paper 電子發票's QR codes on the phone first (exact number, day, total and items with no AI read; the seller's name from 經濟部's register), nothing to tap or see added; any other picture goes to the AI.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 A TPASS (any sub with 有效天數) is counted down on 月曆, with a notice the evening before (18:00, while still out: by 20:00 he's home, too late to renew) and the morning of its last day (08:00); 11-12 the days before at the evening time, that day at the morning time, both the person's to change.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 統計 is a full statistics area: every category with its subs and their share; every useful cut (account and way to pay, a category across months, against the period before, fixed vs day to day, fees, money back, largest, places, weekdays, income vs spending, any dates). 支出 and 收入 are separate views, never netted; the share kept is secondary, under 收入.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-31
cards.text: 10-31 統計 and 帳戶 open dense: one short card, no chart when only one period has anything; groups of a list 16 apart; 分類 a small donut beside one split bar, each line's share and change, subs folded until tapped; a quick-facts strip.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-11-03
cards.text: 11-03 統計's card has room and holds still: 支出/收入 and 篩選 on one row, 日 / 週 / 月 / 年 on its own row; the card leads with the period's name (its menu: recent periods and 自訂期間) and ‹ ›; two figures always; a pick or a step changes words and bars, never the card's size or the page's place. 自訂期間's days are our own centred text over the phone's picker.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Sheets fit their content; nothing that matters below the fold.

cards.title: Money rule, 2026-11-06
cards.text: 11-06 Days are the phone's; NT$ only.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 (22:51) A world story shows how Taiwan's outlets put it (their bar and headlines, tw, joined by a word list builders/news-words.js, never AI); the big world outlets are in, each placed by AllSides. A site that refuses non-browsers is read through Bing News' feed of it (Google News refuses Cloudflare); 民視 through its YouTube channel.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 (22:53) A story's first topic is what most of its headlines name, a second only where 40% name it; in a topic's tab a story's tag is that topic; a tab needs 3 stories; each topic keeps its best 12 past the front's cap; a kind past the sides forms from 2 outlets.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 (22:57) YouTube Shorts are left out; a clip YouTube won't play here says so and opens YouTube; a channel is read only if its clips play elsewhere and aren't mostly Shorts.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 (22:58) A story's sheet keeps ‹ 上一則 · n / N · 下一則 › at its foot; each outlet once a side (its other headlines folded), four a side at first; one company's monthly report is never another's story.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-10
cards.text: 11-10 No one-line AI summary under a headline (it only said the headline again). 11-11 News isn't passive: a search heads 頭條.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 More outlets, Taiwan's and the world's (Jay: "adding even more news outlet from Taiwan and international"), each placed by a source like the rest; Taiwan's places checked against the studies (Jay: "Taiwan news outlet sit majority in middle, that's probably not so true"): TVBS and 東森 moved to 偏藍, 民視 and 三立 to 深綠 by how TEDS 2019's voters see each channel, 關鍵評論網 to 偏綠 by Media Bias/Fact Check's Taiwan ratings (mbfc-tw: its Left-Center is 偏綠, Right-Center 偏藍); an outlet no study has rated stays 中間 marked 依據較弱, never placed by our reading.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 A story's picture is an outlet's photo, never a video's thumbnail while any outlet gave one (Jay: "don't use thumbnail with text"; a channel's frame carries its words burned in): Orbit-Core THUMB_PIC.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 A story's head credits its photo and its clip each to its own outlet (圖：壹蘋 · ▶ 中天的影片), never the photo called the clip; its 影音 row lists every clip, the head's among them, marked 播放中 while it plays (Jay 11-13: "the title video and the only video listed is not the same").

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-12
cards.text: 11-12 The videos inside the articles count (Jay: "get the video embedded in a news web page … Taiwanese news site is the weak spot"): a story's clip may come from its outlets' own pages, only the article's own (never the box beside every article, never a Short); one on the outlet's own player opens on its site.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 Personal like Sports (Jay: "we never really consider orbit news as a reader … kind of like sports's design idea"): what you follow (people and any words, topics, outlets, and the family's holdings and teams) rises through 頭條 and each list, tagged ★ with what of yours it's about (Jay 11-13: "more integrated rather than just an independent section": no separate 你關心的 block), your outlets first in a story's marks; a story read is dimmed, and marked 新進展 when it has big news since; 我的閱讀 nudges toward what your usual side leaves out (你可能錯過). All of it on the phone and the person's own Pass, never sent elsewhere.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 Reading kept in the app (Jay: "just make it more in app"): a story's sheet carries each side's headlines, its clips, 來龍去脈 and 相關新聞; the whole report opens on the outlet's own site (iOS's quick view, closed back to the story). Never an article's text copied: outlets mark them 禁止轉載.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 One story, one event (Jay: "spread text about the news and not so helpful trying to understand it", a world story of 38 outlets over four days holding Pence's 2028 run and Mark Kelly's beside Trump ending the Iran talks): a story keeps the headlines near its core, what drifted from it starts a story of its own where enough outlets carry it. Its title names the event, who did what (never a topic: 伊朗議題受關注), alone in the sheet with the Orbit AI mark; a political story is never also 運動 or 生活 by a word in it (Jay: "why is this sport").

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 A kind with no sides (a game, a storm) lists its outlets in one card, those that wrote most first, never under 偏綠 · 中間 · 偏藍 (Jay: "if this kind of news has no spectrum then don't list them like spectrum"). The world's sports stories are 運動 by their teams and players (the Curry injury was 科技), and Taiwan's sports story joins the world's only a game to a game (the English names Sports' AI gave, news/sport-who.json, went 11-17 with the AI made ahead) (Jay: "why is this Taiwan outlet only"). A foreign person in Chinese only by the name Taiwan's press fixes (translate.js KNOWN), anyone else in English (Scott Colom, never 史考特科洛姆).

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-13
cards.text: 11-13 What's on screen never moves by itself (Jay: opening News "get stuck a few seconds then reshuffle"): lists hold their first-drawn order for the opening, new stories slotting in; only a pull, a follow or the next opening ranks anew. Reads that land together are drawn once.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 影音 is the news told by its clips, not a list of videos (Jay: "Video is basically a list of video super unhelpful … improve it significantly so it's actually about using video to look for news"): a story a card, its best clip playing in place, its title and one line, every outlet's clip on it beside, the whole story a tap away at the same second; one ends, the next story's begins. No second row of kinds under the tabs (it said the tabs again).

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-15
cards.text: 11-15 Headlines are one story only where they share two words or more apart, or name the same game, never one word (Jay: piano pianos and a councillor quitting the KMT joined by 鄭朝方; an engineer's affair, a building firm's win and OpenAI's tools by 工程師; San Antonio's and Tottenham's Spurs): Orbit-Core twoWords, a place's name no word of it. A story's title is the news, never a question, an essay or a column.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-15
cards.text: 11-15 What you haven't seen comes first (Jay: "everytime you open the news it's about what you haven't seen … whether the user actually clicked in any of the article"): back after a while away, a story whose sheet was only opened sits a little lower and rises again with the hours; one whose article was opened goes far down for a day and a half; never reordered while reading. A story is about a holding or a follow by its title or enough of its headlines, never one in passing.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 No Chinese state media (環球時報, CGTN, 新華社), not read, listed or counted (Jay: "remove 中國官媒 we don't need dictatorship to tell us what news is"). Stories about China come from everyone else's reporting.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 AI only for what someone asks for (Jay: "only spend it as I use it but kept fast enough"; later: "make AI feature like this a button to click like we do in orbit law, never spend a penny on AI on things user didn't interact with"): nothing is made ahead, on opening a story or on a finger touching it. Titles are the outlets' own (Google's plain translation for the other language).

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 Nothing is drawn anew under a finger or while the page still moves (Jay: "I can't hold the side bar to scroll … it's refusing my hold"): quietRefresh waits till the page has been still 0.7 s; a story sheet's swipe listens on the sheet alone.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 A row's coverage is its marks, its outlets and its bar, never how many of Taiwan's outlets carry a world story (Jay: "no need to tell me how many Taiwan outlet is reporting this"); the sheet's 台灣媒體怎麼報 shows them.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-17
cards.text: 11-17 No Orbit Words in News (Jay: "Remove Orbit Words from Orbit News"): no words picked from stories, underlined or linked into Words; the family's notebook's vocab.learning isn't read.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-17
cards.text: 11-17 No 重點整理 or 各方怎麼說 (Jay: "Remove 各方怎麼說、重點整理 AI from Orbit News"): a story's sheet has no AI part to tap; who covers it (each side's count, bar and outlets, 報導的媒體) is code's.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-17
cards.text: 11-17 No AI made ahead at all (the ultra stable cut): 預測市場 went (its pairs were the AI's, paused since 11-14, so it had stopped showing anything new) and so did the AI's titles; a title in the other language is the plain translation.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-17
cards.text: 11-17 No 單邊 (Jay: "Remove 單邊 tab as it's really useless"): no tab, no 頭條 section, no 偏藍沒報 mark on a row and no line of who carried it in a story's sheet; the other tabs keep their order and 頭條 still opens first. The builder's blind is read only by 你可能錯過.

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-17
cards.text: 11-17 Orbit Sports' 相關新聞 no longer opens here: News reads no news/sport.json; a story still opens by #s=<id> (Securities' and Law's links).

cards.title: News rule, 2026-11-17
cards.text: 11-17 A story's bar weighs its two ends by how many outlets each has on the page (barOf, story.pool from cleanPage), as if both had as many; the counts in words stay the outlets' own, the middle as counted (Jay: "left news outlet is more than right so often time it looked like all news lean left": the world's 37 left to 23 right made 145 of 223 stories look left, 26 right; weighed, 74 · 80 even · 69). A reading's own bar (你讀的媒體) as counted.

cards.title: Showcase rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Open to all (no Pass, no Add to Home Screen step; an exception to the family) and a real desktop layout besides the phone one: its own side bar on computers (900 px wide, over 520 tall) in place of the kit's rail; pages lay out by the page's width (@container page, wide from 560 px), never the screen's. Check WebKit and Chromium on every screen.

cards.title: Showcase rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Only structure, numbers and demos; plain everyday words for readers who know no tech (problem → idea → result; technical names only inside the 技術細節 fold); Chinese first, English second. The story of how it was made is kept privately for Jay, never in a repo.

cards.title: Showcase rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 Honest framing: Jay sets the direction, the standards and the judgement calls; Claude does the typing. Every number comes from git, never estimated; "on GitHub since", never "began on".

cards.title: Showcase rule, 2026-10-27
cards.text: 10-27 No betting anywhere.

cards.title: Showcase rule, 2026-10-30
cards.text: 10-30 Demos may run the real apps on live data, read-only behind a short showcase pass (showcase.js: from the showcase's address only, per-address and daily caps; past any limit the recording plays); full screen on phones, bug-free, small coach-mark tours.

cards.title: Showcase rule, 2026-11-04
cards.text: 11-04 One page a reader with a few minutes (a teacher, a professor) reads top to bottom; keep the demos and screenshots.

cards.title: Showcase rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 A showcase of the Orbit project, never named a school or 自主學習 piece; no language switch (the browser's language picks it, as on the homepage and the Pass site).

cards.title: Showcase rule, 2026-11-14
cards.text: 11-14 It is Jay's representative piece: the design bar is high, still quick to scan for a professor with minutes. 問 Orbit is everywhere on the page (a pill along the bottom asking about what's on screen), lean on AI (asked only when sent, an answer kept on the device). Demos run in a phone, tablet or computer frame on a computer; while a guided tour runs only its step's target answers a tap (scrolling stays free).
